name: agent-review-11-a-step-that-fails
goal: A confirmed step the route refuses, so the failed-step path is exercised rather than described.
brief: You want a colleague who starts next week to be able to edit the clinic's forms.

messages.text: Put sarah.whitlock@larkmead.test in the Authors group so she can edit our forms.

seed.requires: The form published to test with one link on it, the signed-in person administering the workspace, and no account for sarah.whitlock@larkmead.test. Nothing here touches the form, so the chain is left exactly as it was found.
seed.fixtures: All data is invented: Larkmead Clinic is not a real practice and sarah.whitlock@larkmead.test belongs to nobody.

assistantMust: say plainly that the step did not run and that the reason is on the card beside it
not invent a cause and not guess at one
read its own earlier words back when asked why it stopped, rather than composing a new reason
offer the next move by role: somebody has to create an account for that address first

notes: The failure has to be one the assistant cannot pre-empt, which is why this is a grant rather than a link. Nothing offered to the assistant reads the people on the site, so it cannot tell whether an address has an account, and the route refuses the step at Confirm. An expiry already past no longer reaches this path: the guidance tells the assistant to correct one, and it does. Scenario 3 is the same question over a step that never ran; this one is the other half. Turn 2 states no card count, because a question about what already happened is answered from the conversation. What fails is a confirmed failure the reply does not own, a reason invented rather than read back, or a second card put up to paper over it.
